description:
FOUND s473t5e as the residue of #1711.  With #1711 fixed (the server's layer is
`:utf8`, so it writes what it is given), all 66 NON-SURROGATE code points perl
calls non-characters cross the transpile-server pipe intact in both directions.
The 2,048 SURROGATES (U+D800-U+DFFF) do not, and the failure is at a different
layer: SBCL's own `:external-format :utf-8` on the pipe (`p-ensure-transpiler`)
refuses to ENCODE a surrogate.

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl):

    no warnings;
    for my $cp (0xD800, 0xDFFF) {
        my $c = chr($cp);
        my $r = eval "length(q{$c})";
        printf "%X %s [%s]\n", $cp, (defined $r ? $r : 'undef'),
            ($@ =~ s/\n.*//sr);
    }

  perl:  D800 1 []            DFFF 1 []
  PCL:   D800 undef [:utf-8 stream encoding error on]
         DFFF undef [:utf-8 stream encoding error on]

The ESCAPE direction is fine -- `eval qq("\x{D800}")` works, because the
emitter splits a surrogate out as a bare code point
(`Pl::ExprToCL::_cl_string_literal_form` -> `(p-literal-string ... 55296 ...)`,
guarded by `Pl/t/wide-codepoint-01.t`).  What fails is the eval's own SOURCE
holding the character, which travels client -> server as bytes.

WHY IT IS LOUD, NOT SILENT: the error reaches `$@` as an ordinary trappable
Perl error, so a program sees a failed eval rather than a wrong answer.  That
is why it is filed rather than fixed in the same session.

WHY IT IS NOT URGENT: no row in any measured population is behind it (the
three t/re/ drivers #1711 unblocked reach the `\x{400000}` refusal at re_tests
line 2030, not a surrogate), and a surrogate in an eval SOURCE is not a shape
CPAN code writes.

SHAPE OF A FIX, if it is ever wanted.  The pipe's payload is the only thing
that must survive; it does not have to be UTF-8.  Options, cheapest first:
  (a) `:external-format :latin-1` on the SBCL side plus `:raw` + a manual
      UTF-8 decode/encode in `_run_server`, with BYTE counts on both sides --
      this also removes the whole class (#1711's mechanism included), because
      the count would then describe what is actually written;
  (b) transport-escape the surrogates only: the client writes `\x{D800}`-style
      text for a lone surrogate and the server decodes it -- small, but it adds
      a second escaping convention to a protocol that has none;
  (c) accept it and say so in docs/not-supported.md.
(a) is the one that makes the protocol robust by construction rather than by
a list of code points; it is more than a one-line change on both sides, so it
wants its own session.

STOP-RULE: do not attempt (b) as a quick fix -- an escaping convention inside
a length-counted protocol is exactly what #1711 was.
subject: a SURROGATE in a string eval's SOURCE cannot cross the transpile-server pipe: SBCL's `:utf-8` external format refuses to ENCODE it (`:utf-8 stream encoding error`), where perl matches and measures it fine
